recipes.name: Sloppy Joes inspired by Billy Madison
ingredients: 5 tbsp unsalted butter, softened and divided
spray As needed, neutral oil or nonstick
2 slices *Optional: thick cut bacon, finely minced
1/2 cup red bell pepper, finely chopped
1/2 cup green bell pepper, finely chopped
To taste freshly ground black pepper
6 oz cherry tomatoes (on the vine, preferably)
instructions: For the Manwich
Read the back of the Manwich can. - 1 can Manwich - 1 lb ground beef - 1 package hamburger buns
Enjoy.
For the Potato Buns:
Recipe Credit: King Arthur Flour
Link: https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/recipes/hamburger-potato-buns-recipe

Add the flour, potato flour, milk powder, sugar, salt, yeast, butter, and water to a mixing bowl. - 361 g all purpose flour - 43 g potato flour - 28 g nonfat dry milk powder - 25 g granulated sugar - 8 g kosher salt - 2 tsp instant yeast - 4 tbsp unsalted butter softened and divided - 227 g water (85°F 100°F)
Combine them on low speed using a dough hook attachment. Once homogenous, increase the speed to medium and mix for another 5-7 minutes.
Grease a separate large mixing bowl with neutral oil and place the dough in the bowl. Cover and allow to rest at room temperature for 1 hour. - spray As needed neutral oil or nonstick
Once the dough has risen, lightly grease your work surface with more neutral oil. Turn the dough out of the bowl and divide it into 6 equal portions.
Shape each portion into a taut ball. Place each ball on a medium parchment-lined baking sheet. Make sure each ball is spaced about 1 inch away from each other.
Lightly flatten each ball and cover it with plastic wrap. Allow to rest at room temperature for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until puffed and the buns are slightly touching.
Bake the buns at 350°F for 15 to 20 minutes.
Once golden brown and baked through (190-195°F in the center), remove the buns from the oven and brush with the remaining butter. - 1 tbsp unsalted butter softened and divided
Allow cooling slightly before serving.
For the Babish Sloppy Joe
Combine water, baking soda, and salt in a small bowl and whisk to combine. - 1 tsp water - ½ tsp baking soda - 1 tsp kosher salt
Add baking soda mixture to the ground beef and mix gently with your hands. - 1 pound ground beef (85%)
In a large saucepan, cook minced bacon until browned and the fat has rendered out. - 2 slices *Optional: thick cut bacon finely minced
Using a slotted spoon, remove the bacon bits, leaving the rendered fat in the pan. Remove all but 2 tablespoons of bacon fat.
*If omitting, add 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil.

Add the peppers and onion to the pan. Cook until very tender and lightly browned, about 5 minutes. - ½ cup red bell pepper finely chopped - ½ cup green bell pepper finely chopped - ½ cup onion finely chopped
Push all of the vegetables to the sides of the pan. Add the beef to the center and cook until browned on all sides. Stir periodically to break up any large chunks of beef. - 1 pound ground beef (85%)

Once the beef is cooked, add the garlic cloves, chili powder, and tomato paste. Let cook for 1 minute or until the mixture is no longer soupy. - 2 cloves garlic minced - 1 tbsp chili powder - 2 tbsp tomato paste
Add flour and stir to combine. Cook for 30 more seconds. - ½ tbsp all purpose flour

Add tomato sauce, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, red wine vinegar, paprika, mustard powder, brown sugar, chicken bouillon, and the reserved bacon bits. - 1 cup tomato sauce - ¼ cup ketchup - 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce - 1 tbsp red wine vinegar - 1 tsp chicken bouillon - ½ tsp mustard powder - 1 tsp paprika - 1 ½ tbsp brown sugar
Taste for seasoning, then adds salt and pepper as needed. - To taste kosher salt - To taste freshly ground black pepper
Cook for another 5 minutes, stirring periodically to avoid scorching.
Meanwhile, toast the sliced buns in a medium pan with butter. - For the Potato Bun - 1 tbsp unsalted butter
Fill each bun generously with the sloppy Joe filling.
For the Deconstructed Sloppy Joe
For the Confit Tomatoes
Place cherry tomatoes in a small baking vessel. - 6 oz cherry tomatoes (on the vine preferably)
Add garlic, rosemary, and bay leaf. - 5 garlic cloves peeled - 3 sprigs rosemary - 1 bay leaf
Add enough olive oil to submerge the tomatoes. - As needed olive oil
Bake at 275°F for 1.5 hours, until all of the tomatoes are softened and slightly burst.
Remove the garlic cloves and tomatoes from the oil and place on a cooling rack. Take care not to detach the tomatoes from the vine.
For the Sauce
Add vegetable oil and flour to a large saucepan and whisk to combine. - ½ cup vegetable oil - ½ cup all purpose flour
Heat the roux (flour + vegetable) over low heat. Stir constantly and cook for 20-40 minutes, until it’s the color of dark chocolate.
Add the peppers and onion, cook for about 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender. - ½ cup green bell pepper chopped - ½ cup red bell pepper chopped - ½ cup onion chopped
Add tomato paste and stir to combine. - 3 tbsp tomato paste
Add the beef stock in 3 additions, stirring in-between each addition to make sure the liquid is fully incorporated. - 1 cup homemade beef stock

Add the remaining ingredients and stir to combine. - 2 tbsp ketchup - 1 tbsp red wine vinegar - 2 tbsp brown sugar packed - 1 tsp chili powder - 1 tsp paprika - ½ tsp mustard powder - 1 tsp kosher salt
Strain the sauce with a fine-mesh sieve and reserve both the sauce and the vegetable mixture separately.
For the Burger Bun Crostini
Place the potato bun in the freezer for a minimum of 4 hours. - For the Potato Bun - 1 homemade potato bun
Once fully frozen, slice 2mm thick slices of the bun using a deli slicer.
Place the thinly sliced bun pieces on a small rimmed baking sheet, without parchment.
Gently brush the slices with a thin coating of olive oil. Then, brush the bottom of another small rimmed baking sheet. - 1 tbsp olive oil
Place the oiled baking sheet on top of the bun slices.
Bake at 375°F with convection for 10 minutes.
Once crisp, remove the sheet trays from the oven. Allow the crostinis to cool with the sheet tray still placed on top to avoid curling.
For the Beef Tartare
Finely chop beef, pieces should be smaller than a pea. (Tip: using a very sharp knife will make this step much easier.) - 3 ounces filet mignon (preferably dry aged)

Mix the remaining ingredients together with the chopped beef. Make sure not to over mix the tartare. - 1 confit garlic clove chopped - 2 tbsp reserved vegetable mixture - 2 tsp reserved sauce - ¼ tsp kosher salt - ¼ tsp freshly ground Pepper
Place a 2.5-inch diameter ring mold over the serving plate of your choice. Fill the ring mold with beef tartare and gently remove the ring.
Garnish the tartare with confit tomatoes and crostini. - As needed confit tomatoes - As needed crostini
